solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Writer's block overcome by woman with whiskies?

parts.note: a hen is slang for a woman

indicators.note: the block is covered over by the woman and the whiskies, which close round it

parts.note: ryes are whiskies distilled from rye
a jam is a blockage, as in a traffic jam

explanation.surface: An author stuck for words is rescued by a woman bringing drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome by' means the block is covered by the other two pieces; 'block' suggests writer's block, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The American-born novelist of The Turn of the Screw is a famous author.

clue.text: Male doctor turned to plonk in place of recreation

parts.note: Dr Jekyll turned into the man Mr Hyde in Stevenson's story
to plonk something is to park it, set it down

explanation.surface: A doctor takes to cheap wine somewhere he goes to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plonk' looks like cheap wine but is the verb 'put down'. HYDE PARK is a large park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The big London park is a public space for leisure and walking.

clue.text: Particle from sapling, perhaps, Ken picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a sapling is a new tree, and to ken is to know

explanation.surface: Someone called Ken notices a speck coming off a young tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a man's name but is the Scots verb 'know'.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is a tiny subatomic particle with almost no mass.

clue.text: Even bits of nylon like yarn, initially as yellow

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters of the words nylon like are taken, second, fourth and so on
initially takes the opening letter of the word yarn

explanation.surface: Nylon thread is said to be as yellow as yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even bits of' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'nylon like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resembling egg yolk has its deep golden colour.

clue.text: Passage the writer is to broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out on air, so the sound counts

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I, and 'is to' means will, giving I'll

explanation.surface: A writer announces a passage they plan to put out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer is to' means 'I will', shortened to I'll.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or plane, is a passage.

clue.text: Typical of hikers to leave rocks on track

indicators.note: rocks means shakes up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Walkers are told to leave stones on the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hikers' are things that hike, that is lift up, not walkers; 'rocks' shuffles TO LEAVE into ELEVATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevatory means serving to raise, and a hiker here is anything that raises.

clue.text: Well set for printing

definitions.meaning: a fountain or spring, the old sense of the word
a set of type in one size and style

explanation.surface: Something ready to go off to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a spring of water and a typeface used in printing.

clue.text: Hardy, maybe, but not a survivor

parts.note: O is zero, nothing, read here as not
one who lives on is a liver

explanation.surface: Someone tough who still didn't make it through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like an adjective but is Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Hardy was the comedian partnered with Stan Laurel, so Hardy is an example of the first name.

clue.text: All the same mass equally? More?

parts.note: tho, short for though, means all the same
M is the symbol for mass
as means equally, as in as tall

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether everything weighs the same, or more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, Henry VIII's chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas More, the Tudor statesman and saint, has this first name.

clue.text: Mostly far from fair for Ape to assume place of Man

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: to ape someone is to do as they do

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: far from fair, plain-looking, is ugly

explanation.surface: An unattractive ape takes a man's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, not a human; 'Ape' is the verb 'imitate'.
explanation.definitionFit: This town is the capital of the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Out of her mind, poor Maxine, with love

indicators.note: poor suggests badly made, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Maxine has gone mad with love, poor thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of her mind' looks like madness but translates the Latin literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means sincerely, literally from the mind or heart.

clue.text: He'd produce huge vegetable dipped in gin

indicators.note: the gin is dipped into the name, so taking that spirit out again leaves him

parts.note: a giant onion is a huge vegetable
the spirit is taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook would make a huge vegetable dish soaked in gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'he, with gin dipped in, would produce GIANT ONION': the man's name plus G, I, N. 'He'd' is the definition, a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is a man's name, so 'he' stands for this fellow.

clue.text: Fellow from a country's borders

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head

indicators.note: borders picks out the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A man comes over a nation's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives PER, as in 'so much a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy is a man's name, so it can stand for a fellow.

clue.text: French in hymn? A sore point!

parts.note: en is French for in
an anthem is a hymn

explanation.surface: French in a church song is a touchy subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sore point' looks like a touchy topic but is a literal sore.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical term is an eruption on a mucous membrane, a sore spot inside the body.

clue.text: Doctor from East keeps coming upon strange chemical substance

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so the first piece goes round the second
in an across entry, coming from the east means read right to left
strange signals the words are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: An eastern doctor keeps finding a peculiar chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from East' reads right to left in an across light; 'strange' makes INGCOMPOUN of COMING UPON.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule whose atoms form a closed loop, like benzene, is a type of chemical.

clue.text: City that was my home before leaving there

parts.note: cor is an exclamation like my!
in means at home

indicators.note: leaving signals the second word departs from the first

parts.note: the word taken as written
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the city they lived in before moving away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation of surprise, not a possessive; 'before' is not a link but the word removed from 'there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth is an ancient Greek city on the isthmus joining the Peloponnese.

clue.text: Close three successive letters penning articles about Chomsky

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the letters surround what follows

parts.note: M, N, O follow one another in the alphabet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the name

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, twice over here
Noam Chomsky is the American linguist

explanation.surface: Three letters in a row nearly enclose some writing about a linguist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb but means close-quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish phrase means hand to hand, so a fight at close quarters.

clue.text: Sri Lankan cricketer once turned up in Calcutta, Patagonia

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A former cricketer appears in Calcutta and South America.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turned up' reads the letters bottom to top; 'in' marks them as concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Marvan Atapattu captained Sri Lanka at Test cricket and later coached the side.

clue.text: Container of cardboard or wood containing gin

indicators.note: containing means the wood holds the next piece inside

parts.note: teak is a hardwood
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: A box made of card or timber holding a bottle of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink but is a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetra Pak is the brand of laminated carton used for milk and juice.

clue.text: Possible holder of fine tip from bookmaker, after the other lot bet recklessly

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the other is slang for sex, so someone after it is randy

indicators.note: recklessly says the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: A tipster takes a gamble after the other punters bet wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' is a fine brandy, not a penalty; 'the other' is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine is a French term for good brandy, which a bottle of that spirit would hold.

clue.text: Turn before green light comes up, keeping right in general

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a nod is approval, a green light

explanation.surface: Driving instructions: turn before the light goes green, keeping right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' makes DON; 'green light' is approval, not a traffic signal. Gordon of Khartoum was a Victorian British general.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Gordon was the Victorian army general killed at Khartoum.

clue.text: Prince and leading journalist campaigning with Duke

parts.note: an editor, ED, leads a newspaper's journalists
campaigning is being at war

explanation.surface: A prince and a top reporter campaign alongside a duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Edward is the youngest son of Elizabeth II, one of several royals of the name.

clue.text: Grand opening poem names a quiet American humorist

indicators.note: opening means cutting open, so the letter goes inside the poem

parts.note: an ode is a poem
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
N is the abbreviation for name, doubled for the plural
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A grand opening poem name-checks a quiet American comic writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like 'first' but means G splits ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogden Nash was an American writer famous for comic light verse.

clue.text: New base for hotel that regenerated after cuts at the top

definitions.text: that regenerated after cuts at the top

indicators.note: a new base means the bottom letter of a down entry is swapped

parts.note: a hydro is a spa hotel

explanation.surface: A hotel that was rebuilt on new foundations after cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hotel' is HYDRO, a British spa hotel; A replaces its last letter. The definition describes the beast whose heads regrew when cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lernaean monster grew new heads whenever Heracles chopped one off.

clue.text: Transported first class by return, for what it's worth

indicators.note: by return means coming back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: rapt means carried away, transported
A is first class, as in A1

explanation.surface: Delighted to be in first class on the way back, for what it's worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' means enraptured, not carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A share at face value trades for exactly its nominal worth.

clue.text: Arab leader needing trailer for something to sit on

parts.note: the backside, or ass, is what one sits on
a trailer is an advert, ad

explanation.surface: A head of state needs a towed cart for his seating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' looks like a towed vehicle but is a film advert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Assads, father and son, ruled Syria for decades.

clue.text: Children play cops once ready

indicators.note: cops means catches, so the play takes in the next piece

parts.note: a drama is a play

explanation.surface: Kids play at cops and robbers, once they are ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for cash; 'once' says this money is no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Greek currency was cash, ready money, before the euro.

clue.text: Bureau chief will do for PC

parts.note: a bureau is a writing desk
top means chief, head

explanation.surface: An office boss will settle for a police constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a police officer but is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer made to sit on a desk is a personal computer.

clue.text: ____? Last of fig leaves prompt!

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so a letter departs the word

parts.note: a nudge is a prompt

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of fig

explanation.surface: The final fig leaf falls away: what are you then?
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb; the whole clue is the picture of a statue losing its fig leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Once the last fig leaf goes, a figure is left unclothed.

clue.text: Godfather with a chance to consume skin of dead bird apparently brought to life

parts.note: a don is a Mafia godfather

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the chance swallows the next letters

parts.note: luck is chance

indicators.note: the skin of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss eats a dead bird's skin, then it comes back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cartoon bird, animated so 'brought to life'.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's cartoon duck is a bird animated on screen, so seemingly alive.
